ELI5: Why do people seem to taste food differently?

I would assume it has something to do with the fact that everyone is genetically different and so everyone has unique taste buds. It probably also has something to do with perception and foods that people are used to growing up with.

It's likely not so much genes, but developmental differences. People recognize colors [maybe not "perceive", but definitely identity] differently depending on the language they grow up in, as the language define the color "categories." I wouldn't be surprised if language and other social/developmental things affect taste perception as well. I'm pretty sure you're taste buds change as you age as well.

You may honestly have conscious control, to a degree, simply by thinking of related flavors while eating something. I imagine this plays into why things like beer or wine have so many "complex" flavors.
